sets.relationshipLabel: a tool and the exact action it exists to perform
sets.explanation: A chisel exists to carve just as a lathe exists to turn — each tool is defined by its one signature motion.

sets.relationshipLabel: an object placed to stop the mark it would otherwise cause
sets.explanation: A coaster exists to stop a stain and a felt pad exists to stop a scratch — both are small guards against damage from the object they sit under.
baitTags: object-mark pairing could be mistaken for tool-action

sets.relationshipLabel: a surface that conceals the cheaper or structural material beneath it
sets.explanation: Veneer hides particleboard and upholstery hides a frame — both are the visible skin covering the cheaper structure underneath.
baitTags: upholstery/frame could look like a synonym pair for furniture parts

sets.relationshipLabel: an older, specific name for the same everyday furniture piece
sets.explanation: A davenport is an old-fashioned word for a sofa, and a hassock is an old-fashioned word for an ottoman — each pair names the same object across generations.
baitTags: dated vocabulary reads as unrelated furniture terms at first

glossary.definition: A thickly padded, cushioned stool for resting your feet or sitting on low to the ground.

definitions.definition: A sharp-edged hand tool you push or tap with a mallet to cut into wood or stone.
To shape something by cutting away bits of material, usually wood.
A machine that spins material around so a tool can shape it evenly.
To shape something by spinning it while cutting, giving it a smooth round form.
A small mat you set a cup on to protect the surface underneath.
A discolored mark left behind, often from spilled liquid.
A soft little sticker you put on furniture legs to protect the floor.
A thin mark or groove left when something scrapes across a surface.
A thin decorative layer of nice wood glued over a cheaper surface.
A cheap board made of pressed wood chips and glue, often hidden under nicer material.
The fabric or padding covering that makes furniture soft and finished-looking.
The sturdy skeleton structure that gives a piece of furniture its shape.
An old-fashioned word people used to use for a couch.
A long cushioned seat meant for more than one person to sit or lounge on.
A thickly padded, cushioned stool for resting your feet or sitting on low to the ground.
A low cushioned footstool you can rest your feet on or use as extra seating.
